title: Burst-aware prefetch slack controller and kernel hinting
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Implement a controller that dynamically adjusts prefill "slack" (how much prefetching we do ahead of decode) and emits lightweight kernel hints to the admission/batcher layer based on observed burstiness and attention profile. Goal is to reduce P99 tail latency for multi-tenant continuous batching workloads while preserving throughput and modestly improving unit cost.

Background:
- Continuous batching currently struggles with short, highly-bursty interactive streams: admission either over-prefetches (wasting KV/caching work) or under-prefetches (creating decode stalls and long tail latency when requests collide).
- Kernel selection logic is conservative: variants optimized for short sequences or quantized paths are chosen only after stable signals; this increases decode latency for opportunistic short requests.

Scope / What we'll build:
1) Prefetch Slack Controller: a runtime component that computes a per-queue "slack" value (number of tokens to pre-warm / prefill per request) using exponentially-weighted burst metrics and per-customer latency budgets. Slack is reduced during sustained bursts to avoid KV thrash, and increased when steady-state low-latency is achievable.
2) Kernel Hinting API: an internal hint type included with admission metadata (e.g., prefer-small-kernel, quantized-friendly, attention-sparse) so the kernel scheduler can prioritize compact execution paths for requests likely to be short or attention-light. Hints do not mandate selection — they update scorer weights.
3) Prefill/Decode Tie-breaker: a scheduling rule that prefers prefill-first for requests with high slack but will optionally speculative-decode a tiny prefix on short requests to reduce p95/p99 latency when admission backlog is low.
4) Fairness credits and tail guard: per-tenant credit buckets to guarantee a minimum admission share during spikes; a tail-guard path that can fall back to a smaller-model-compatible kernel variant when decode queue growth exceeds threshold.

Success metrics (measured on canary cluster and benchmark suite):
- P99 end-to-end generation latency for interactive traces: target -35% relative to baseline.
- P95 latency: target -20%.
- Median latency: no more than +5% regression.
- Throughput (tokens/s): within -3% of baseline under steady load.
- Cost/unit (GPU token cost): neutral or improved due to better KV reuse.

Design notes and heuristics:
- Burst detection: EWMA of arrival rate plus a short-term variance score; tunable thresholds per-customer.
- Slack computation: slack = clamp(base_slack * (1 - burst_factor) + prewarm_bonus, min_slack, max_slack). Base_slack derives from model's typical sequence distribution and customer SLA.
- Kernel hint weights: hints modify kernel scoring by small deltas (e.g., +10% score for prefer-small-kernel) so existing kernel confidence still dominates unless signals are strong.
- Attention optimizations signaled in hints: attention-sparse triggers combined KV packing and grouped prefetch; attention-dense discourages aggressive prefetching (to avoid heavy KV work).
- Speculative prefix-decode: decode first N tokens in an isolated fast-path kernel when the admission queue is empty for >Xms and request looks likely to be short (entropy prediction model). If speculative decode fails, continue normal path but cancel speculative work accounting for wasted tokens in metrics.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Risk: over-aggressive slack reduction can increase p50 for long-running streams if KV cache misses increase. Mitigation: conservative per-model min_slack and rollout in canary.
- Risk: kernel hints could bias scheduler to suboptimal kernels for complex sequences. Mitigation: hint weights small and we collect misprediction telemetry for automated de-biasing.
- Risk: per-tenant credits add scheduling complexity and state. We will implement lightweight token-bucket style credits backed by in-memory sharded store; fall back to global policy if state missing.

Telemetry and tests (see telemetry_queries below):
- New Grafana panels for slack distribution per-tenant, kernel-hint adoption rate, speculative prefix success rate, wasted speculative tokens, per-kernel average decode latency, and per-tenant P99 generation latency.
- Load tests: re-run interactive tracebench with short-burst mixes (70% short <20 token requests, 30% long) at 1.2x baseline QPS; synthetic KV stress tests to measure cache churn.

Acceptance criteria:
- All unit and integration tests pass in CI; canary rollout running for 72h with no latency regressions above defined thresholds.
- Feature has telemetry dashboards populated and alerts for: kernel mismatch rate > 5%, speculative wastage > 1% tokens, per-tenant credit starvation event count > 0 (indicates misconfiguration).
- Docs: design doc merged to Confluence; internal SDK/marshalling changes documented for admission metadata.
acceptance_criteria:
- P99 latency reduced by >=30% on interactive short-burst benchmark
- No more than 5% kernel misselection rate reported during canary
- Canary run 72h with no alert fires for speculative-waste or credit-starvation
- Rollout plan validated and feature flag gated
design_decisions:
- Conservative hinting: hints adjust kernel scorer but don't override it
- Use EWMA+variance for burst detection instead of burst-only counters to handle noisy workloads
- Speculative prefix-decode limited to a small token window and isolated fast-path kernel to bound wasted work
- Per-tenant credits implemented as leaky-bucket to avoid unbounded state
- Telemetry-first approach: instrument all decisions and expose raw counters for offline analysis
rollout_plan:
1) Unit + integration tests + perf harness locally (2 weeks)
2) Canary on 3 mid-size customers under feature flag (runtime-2.4 canary pool) for 72h
3) Expand canary to 10% traffic with continuous observation and automated rollback thresholds
4) Global rollout with gradual ramp over one week if metrics stable
5) Turn on per-customer tunables (min_slack) for enterprise customers after review
telemetry_queries: bigquery:SELECT tenant, percentile_latency(queries, 0.99) FROM tracebench WHERE workload='interactive-short' GROUP BY tenant
tasks: T1: Implement slack controller module and config proto
T2: Add kernel hint metadata wire format and marshaller in admission path
T3: Integrate hint weights into kernel scorer and unit tests
T4: Implement per-tenant credit buckets and fairness guard
T5: Build speculative prefix-decode fast-path and safety cancellations
T6: Add telemetry counters and Grafana dashboard panels
T7: Perf benchmarks and canary orchestration scripts
T8: Documentation and runbook for rollback/observability
